items.title: OpenAI’s 700W Jalapeño ASIC outpaces 1,400W Nvidia flagship GPU — claims up to 1.9x throughput per kilowatt and 3.6x lower latency, co-developed with Broadcom
items.description: OpenAI arrived at Hot Chips on Tuesday with benchmarks claiming its first in-house chip beats Nvidia's GB300.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Just over one week after Nvidia agreed to backstop up to $105 billion in financing for its data centers, OpenAI arrived at Hot Chips on Tuesday with benchmarks claiming its first in-house chip beats Nvidia's GB300. Jalapeño, the inference ASIC OpenAI co-developed with Broadcom, delivered 1.5 times to 1.9 times more throughput per kilowatt and 1.7 times to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency than Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 rack systems on SemiAnalysis's public InferenceX suite, with a 700W part going up against accelerators rated at 1,200W and 1,400W. OpenAI plans to begin deploying the chip in its own data centers later this year.The tests covered three open models: GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 670B, and Moonshot AI's 1-trillion-parameter Kimi K2.5, with OpenAI reporting its widest leads at low-latency operating points, where it claims 8.6 times to 104.3 times more throughput per kilowatt at the GB300's fastest previous time-between-tokens settings. (Image credit: OpenAI)OpenAI normalized the results to each accelerator's published package TDP, though it said Jalapeño's measured sustained power stayed at or below 550W in testing. An appendix comparison using all-in utility power per accelerator, 1.18kW for Jalapeño against 2.55kW for the GB300, produces narrower gaps, as does pitting Jalapeño against a GB300 running multi-token prediction, where the peak efficiency lead shrinks to roughly 1.5 times.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Jalapeño wasn't tested against Vera Rubin, the Nvidia platform that's slated to power the first gigawatt of Nvidia systems OpenAI agreed to deploy in the second half of 2026. The chip also doesn't train models, the workload where Nvidia's hardware remains unchallenged. In addition, the major comparisons ran Jalapeño's single-token prediction against GB300 configurations doing the same, even though Nvidia deployments commonly use multi-token prediction in production. SemiAnalysis, which said it ran InferenceX with OpenAI engineers in the company's lab, described the part as "beating every Nvidia, AMD, and Google chip we have been able to test."Each Jalapeño package, unveiled in June after a nine-month RTL-to-tapeout cycle, pairs its compute die with six HBM4 stacks, totaling 216 GiB at 15.4 TB/s. The GB300 carries 288GB of HBM3E at a 1,400W rating, so per watt of rated power, OpenAI's chip packs roughly 50% more memory. The company's Hot Chips presentation states that the main bottleneck its architecture targets is exposing aggregate HBM bandwidth, not adding more of it. You may like Broadcom and OpenAI unveil custom-built Jalapeño inference processor Behind the scenes at Nvidia's Engineering SuperLab Nvidia weighs $250 billion guarantee so OpenAI can lease SoftBank's 10-gigawatt Ohio campus, report claims That memory is of course the tightest commodity in the semiconductor industry. Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron have sold their HBM capacity through 2027, a shortage so severe that Nvidia is reportedly testing cut-down Rubin Ultra configurations with as little as 192GB, and SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung has warned that 2027 will be the worst year of the crunch. Micron told the same Hot Chips conference on August 23 that HBM consumes roughly three times the wafer area of DDR5 for equivalent capacity, a penalty that widens with each generation. Scaling Jalapeño across the 10GW deployment agreement that OpenAI signed with Broadcom last October would make the company a substantial new claimant to HBM4 supply, which Nvidia currently dominates through multi-year allocation deals with SK hynix. A second-generation chip is approaching tapeout, expected within months, according to Bloomberg, and concept work on a third generation is underway. The first part reportedly uses a TSMC 3nm-class process, keeping OpenAI in the same wafer, memory, and advanced packaging queues as Blackwell and Rubin for the foreseeable future.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsOpenAI is procuring those inputs while deepening its financial dependence on the company it just benchmarked. On August 17, Nvidia agreed to provide up to $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI-leased data center campus in Ohio. "Nvidia is a really good partner, and we continue to need a lot of Nvidia," Richard Ho, OpenAI's vice president of hardware, told Bloomberg in an interview following the announcement. items.titleZh: OpenAI’s 700W Jalapeño ASIC outpaces 1,400W Nvidia flagship GPU — claims up to 1.9x throughput per kilowatt and 3.6x lower latency, co-developed with Broadcom
items.descriptionZh:
在Nvidia同意为OpenAI租赁的数据中心提供高达1050亿美元融资支持仅一周后，OpenAI于本周二在Hot Chips大会上携自研芯片高调亮相，并公布了首批基准测试成绩，声称其首款自研推理芯片在关键指标上已超越Nvidia的GB300。这款名为“Jalapeño”的推理专用集成电路（ASIC）由OpenAI与博通联合开发，在SemiAnalysis公开的InferenceX基准套件测试中，Jalapeño每千瓦功耗的吞吐量是Nvidia GB200和GB300整机系统的1.5至1.9倍，端到端延迟则低1.7至3.6倍。值得注意的是，Jalapeño的额定功耗为700W，而对比的Nvidia加速器功耗分别为1200W和1400W。OpenAI计划于今年晚些时候开始将这款芯片部署到自家的数据中心中。

测试覆盖了三款开源模型：GPT-OSS 120B、DeepSeek R1 670B以及月之暗面的万亿参数模型Kimi K2.5。OpenAI表示，其在低延迟工作点上的优势最为显著——在GB300此前最快的token间时间设置下，Jalapeño每千瓦功耗的吞吐量高出8.6倍至104.3倍。需要说明的是，OpenAI将结果统一归一化到各加速器公布的封装热设计功耗（TDP）上，但OpenAI透露，在测试中Jalapeño的实际持续功耗始终维持在550W或以下。附录中的对比显示，如果改用每块加速器的全口径电力功耗（Jalapeño为1.18kW，GB300为2.55kW），差距将明显收窄；而当Jalapeño与启用了多token预测（MTP）的GB300对战时，其峰值效率优势更是缩小至约1.5倍。

此外，这一对比存在若干重要前提。Jalapeño并未与Nvidia下一代平台Vera Rubin同台竞技——后者正是OpenAI同意在2026年下半年部署的首个吉瓦级Nvidia系统所采用的核心平台。Jalapeño也无法用于模型训练，而训练正是Nvidia硬件目前无可撼动的领域。同时，主要对比是在Jalapeño的单token预测模式与GB300同样采用单token预测的配置之间进行的，尽管Nvidia在生产环境中普遍使用多token预测。负责测试的SemiAnalysis表示，该测试由OpenAI工程师在公司实验室中运行InferenceX完成，并评价道，这款芯片“击败了我们能够测试到的所有Nvidia、AMD和Google芯片”。

Jalapeño的硬件规格在2025年6月即已公开，其从RTL设计到流片仅用了九个月。每个Jalapeño封装将计算die与六个HBM4堆栈配对，总容量达216 GiB，带宽为15.4 TB/s。相比之下，GB300搭载288GB HBM3E，额定功耗1400W；按每瓦额定功率计算，OpenAI的芯片内存容量高出约50%。OpenAI在Hot Chips的展示中指出，该架构所要解决的核心瓶颈是“暴露”聚合HBM带宽，而非单纯增加更多内存容量。

内存恰恰是当前半导体行业最为紧缺的资源。三星、SK海力士和美光已经将HBM产能售罄至2027年，短缺程度之严重，以至于有报道称Nvidia正在测试内存仅为192GB的削减版Rubin Ultra配置。SK海力士CEO郭鲁正（Kwak Noh-jung）警告称，2027年将是供应紧张最严重的一年。美光也在8月23日的Hot Chips会议上表示，同等容量下，HBM消耗的晶圆面积约为DDR5的三倍，且这一代价随每一代工艺而扩大。OpenAI若按照去年10月与博通签署的10GW部署协议扩展Jalapeño的规模，将使其成为HBM4供应的重大新需求方——而这一市场目前由Nvidia通过与SK海力士的多年期分配协议所主导。据彭博社报道，Jalapeño的第二代芯片已接近流片，预计数月内完成，第三代的概念设计也已启动。第一代芯片采用台积电3nm级工艺，这意味着在可预见的未来，OpenAI将与Blackwell和Rubin系列共享同一条晶圆、内存及先进封装供应链。

值得注意的是，OpenAI在采购这些关键部件的同时，也在加深对刚刚被其基准测试击败的Nvidia的财务依赖。8月17日，Nvidia同意为OpenAI在俄亥俄州租用的数据中心园区提供最高1050亿美元的融资。OpenAI硬件副总裁Richard Ho在公告后接受彭博社采访时表示：“Nvidia是一个非常优秀的合作伙伴，我们仍然需要大量的Nvidia产品。”这一表态凸显了OpenAI在自研芯片与外部依赖之间的微妙平衡——一边是试图借助自研ASIC打破算力垄断的技术雄心，另一边则是短期内依然无法摆脱对Nvidia生态和资本的深度绑定。

items.title: Hot Chips 2026: Intel details cutting-edge tech in entry-level Wildcat Lake — value-focused 18A chips necessitated UCIe integration
items.description: Intel's Wildcat Lake is competing in the budget laptop market, but it takes a very different approach, leveraging a UCIe interconnect and Intel's latest 18A node.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter This Tom's Hardware Premium article is free to read with a Tom's Hardware account; no payment necessary. We're offering free access from August 23 to 26 so you can read all of our reporting from Hot Chips.Intel's Wildcat Lake is unassuming, launching with the message that it was a cutting-edge alternative to the MacBook Neo with Intel's latest node and some trimmings around the edges. Although Wildcat Lake is, indeed, a budget part with major concessions to reach a market increasingly pushed to the side by powerful PC hardware, it also comes with a major innovation: UCIe.The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) specification first debuted in 2022, coincidentally around the time that planning around Wildcat Lake began. Both AMD and Intel have rallied behind UCIe as an open interconnect communications standard, though they've primarily relied on their own chiplet communication technology like AMD's Infinity Fabric. In Wildcat Lake, Intel leveraged UCIe to reduce cost. Further, it was a key technology that allowed Wildcat Lake to exist in the first place.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Opening the Hot Chips 2026 presentation, Intel's Lance Hacking, lead engineer on Wildcat Lake, said the company had the choice between a monolithic design or a basic, low-cost Multi-Chip Package (MCP). Intel has Foveros for advanced 2.5D and 3D packaging, but for a budget part like Wildcat Lake, that wasn't an option.Choosing to leverage UCIe over an MCP design shaped the Wildcat Lake we have today, setting a roadmap for where Intel could cut compute to save cost and in areas where it would need to optimize to fit the necessary communication channels for the two chiplets. You may like Hot Chips 2026: Intel dives deep on Crescent Island AI accelerator Intel reportedly no longer working on 6-core Nova Lake mobile SKU, alleges new rumor Intel Arc G3 interview transcript — Intel's Senior Product Director talks new handheld chips, Arrow Lake Refresh, and RTX Spark UCIe integration in Intel Wildcat LakeAs Hacking explained during his presentation, budget parts usually involve an N-1 design. You leverage older IP, trim around the edges to improve the economics of yields, and repackage it as a mainstream part. Wildcat Lake is different in that regard. It's taking Intel's latest, most advanced, and most expensive IP for compute and applying it to the budget domain. (Image credit: Intel)With 18A at the center of the compute and ISMC's N6 handling the I/O die, Intel decided to make an MCP, which comes with some considerations. Advanced packaging allows designers to spend less die space on interconnects and use less power. With UCIe, Wildcat Lake's interconnect is 70% larger than that on Panther Lake, and even then, Intel says the change was worth it from a cost perspective. (Image credit: Intel)Outside of space, power was the primary concern with using UCIe. Battery life, especially for a budget part meant to handle lighter workloads, is extremely important, and UCIe brings increased power demands. UCIe die-to-die is packetized, which led to a challenging design point, particularly around the display.Intel says that idle systems without panel self-refresh were the "biggest power concern," as display signals need to cross the UCIe connection. To address the issue, Intel says it built a buffer to hold panel refreshes while the system was idle. This buffer is before the UCIe link, and it serves as an additional output buffer alongside the typical display buffer between the memory controller and display engine. (Image credit: Intel)Without a base die for interconnect communication, UCIe also represents a large increase in die area. Intel trimmed a lot on both the compute and I/O dies to account for UCIe. What to read next Hot Chips 2026: Intel Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' comes with up to 256 P-cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache Intel will reportedly upgrade to an 8-core config for its Wildcat Lake refresh next year Intel VP Robert Hallock sets Nova Lake expectations, teases return to Raptor Lake for DDR4 platforms — our full 1:1 interview transcript (Image credit: Intel)On the compute die, Intel trimmed down everything. Four Xe cores dropped to two, and without a dedicated ray tracing accelerator, the NPU went from three tiles to a single tile, and the memory subsystem was downgraded to a 64-bit bus, with lower maximum speeds and lower capacity. As mentioned, there were a lot of cuts in the display engine, which was a primary concern for die space and power.Intel uses three display pipelines instead of four, opting for HBR3 as opposed to the massive bandwidth offered with UHBR20. That still provides 4K60 and can drive three external displays, which is plenty for a device in the class that Wildcat Lake is targeting. Trimming down the compute die allowed Intel to claw back 38% of its die space. (Image credit: Intel)On the I/O die, Intel claimed back 15% die area by removing the camera PHY, reducing PCIe and USB support, and slimming down the audio engine. The camera was completely removed, placing the onus on OEMs to integrate their own controllers. (Image credit: Intel)UCIe 3.0 is capable of up to a data rate of 64 GT/s, but Intel capped the transfer rate in Wildcat Lake at 8 GT/s. That still allowed Wildcat Lake to support mainstream PCIe 4 SSDs and 4K60 external displays, but running at a lower data rate reduces bit-rate errors and therefore allowed Intel to remove some bit-correction systems.Reducing the cost of Wildcat Lake (Image credit: Intel)Cutting down the compute and I/O dies saves money, but there are several other considerations when talking about the cost of a mobile SoC like Wildcat Lake. The economics need to work in the final product, which Intel touched on in its Hot Chips presentation, both from the perspective of the total bill of materials for OEMs and the yield/loss rate. (Image credit: Intel)The big factor in cost savings was the elimination of the base die, which not only reduces raw material costs but also comes with the yield upside, without advanced packaging. (Image credit: Intel)As usual, Intel bins Wildcat Lake into different SKUs, though it was careful to only attempt recovery where it could. For instance, it could package a single working P-core as a Core 3 304 instead of a 320. However, it didn't attempt recovery in areas that would compromise key design points of Wildcat Lake.For instance, it didn't attempt recovery on LPE clusters and I/O, as they're critical components of Wildcat Lake. The goal, according to Intel, was to create a stack that customers actually wanted to buy while trying to maximize yields where possible. (Image credit: Intel)Intel also considered the full bill of materials for Wildcat Lake. Intel integrated Wi-Fi 7 and a USB PD controller, cutting costs for OEMs to integrate their own controllers. Perhaps the biggest point of savings was in memory, using a much slimmer bus and a 6-layer PCB as opposed to eight layers. Extending off the chart above is Project Firefly, Intel's initiative to leverage the mobile supply chain for budget laptops.Interestingly, Intel also included an area that led to higher cost but met the design goals of Wildcat Lake, that being a dedicated power rail for the LPE cluster. The "low-power island," as Intel calls its LPE cluster, is critical to Wildcat Lake considering every SKU comes with only one or two P-cores. That dedicated power rail allows the vast majority of lightweight workloads to run on the LPE cluster and earn back battery life.Wildcat Lake is one of the more interesting consumer launches we've seen in the past year. There's the MacBook Neo and Snapdragon C competing in the same space, but both use mobile SoCs in the traditional N-1 design point for budget platforms. Wildcat Lake is different, based on Intel's latest node, and leveraging newer open standards to achieve a lower price. That's why it won a Tom's Hardware innovation award for 2026, after all.Full Intel Wildcat Lake Hot Chips 2026 presentation Image 1 of 19 (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) (Image credit: Intel) Image 1 of 19 View Original Image 2 of 19 View Original Image 3 of 19 View Original Image 4 of 19 View Original Image 5 of 19 View Original Image 6 of 19 View Original Image 7 of 19 View Original Image 8 of 19 View Original Image 9 of 19 View Original Image 10 of 19 View Original Image 11 of 19 View Original Image 12 of 19 View Original Image 13 of 19 View Original Image 14 of 19 View Original Image 15 of 19 View Original Image 16 of 19 View Original Image 17 of 19 View Original Image 18 of 19 View Original Image 19 of 19 View Original

items.titleZh: Hot Chips 2026: Intel details cutting-edge tech in entry-level Wildcat Lake — value-focused 18A chips necessitated UCIe integration
items.descriptionZh:
Intel在Hot Chips 2026大会上详细披露了其新一代低功耗处理器Wildcat Lake的设计细节，这款产品最大的亮点在于首次将UCIe（通用小芯片互连标准）应用于主流预算级移动SoC，以极具创新性的方式实现了成本控制。Wildcat Lake的定位是应对MacBook Neo和骁龙C系列等竞品的入门级产品，但与传统预算芯片采用前代成熟IP（N-1设计）的做法截然不同，它直接采用了Intel最先进的18A制程工艺来制造计算die，同时搭配ISMC的N6工艺制造I/O die，通过多芯片封装（MCP）形式组合。

UCIe规范于2022年首次推出，恰好是Wildcat Lake开始规划的时间。尽管AMD和Intel都公开支持UCIe作为开放的小芯片互连标准，但此前双方在实际产品中主要依赖自家的互连技术（如AMD的Infinity Fabric）。Wildcat Lake是Intel首次在大规模量产消费级芯片中真正用UCIe替代传统的高级封装互连方案。Intel原本面临两个选择：单芯片设计或低成本MCP封装。由于Foveros等先进2.5D/3D封装技术成本过高，不适用于预算级产品，最终决定在MCP中采用UCIe作为die间通信协议。

然而，这一选择带来了显著的工程挑战。首先，UCIe互连的物理面积比Intel自家Panther Lake上的方案大了约70%，为此工程师不得不在计算die和I/O die上大量精简功能来腾出空间。其次，功耗是最大的忧虑，尤其对于轻负载为主的预算产品，电池续航至关重要。UCIe的die-to-die通信采用数据包化传输，导致空闲时显示信号也需要穿越UCIe链路，带来了严重的待机功耗问题。Intel为此专门设计了一个位于UCIe链路之前的缓冲器，在系统空闲时暂存面板刷新数据，配合面板自刷新机制以降低功耗。此外，由于没有基础die来承载互连通信，UCIe也增大了整体die面积。

为了平衡这些代价，Intel对计算die进行了大刀阔斧的削减：Xe核从4个减至2个，并移除了独立光线追踪加速器；NPU从3个tile减至1个；内存子系统降至64位总线，并降低最大速率和容量；显示引擎从4条管道减至3条，采用HBR3而非超高带宽的UHBR20，不过依然支持4K60输出和三个外接显示器，足以满足目标设备需求。这些削减合计收回了38%的die面积。在I/O die方面，Intel通过移除摄像头PHY、减少PCIe和USB支持、精简音频引擎，节省了15%的die面积。摄像头功能被完全移除，将相关控制器集成工作交给了OEM厂商。

数据传输速率方面，UCIe 3.0规范支持最高64 GT/s，但Wildcat Lake人为限制在8 GT/s。这虽然降低了理论带宽，但足以支持主流的PCIe 4.0 SSD和4K60外接显示，同时更低的速率显著降低了误码率，使Intel可以省去部分纠错电路，进一步节省成本与功耗。

成本控制是Wildcat Lake的另一大核心。最大节省来自取消基础die（base die），这既降低了原材料成本，也因避免了高级封装带来的良率损失而获得良率收益。Intel对芯片进行了细致的分级回收，例如将只有单个可用P-core的芯片封装为Core 3 304而非320型号，但对于LPE（低功耗E核）簇和I/O等关键组件，则不做回收，以确保产品的核心设计目标不被破坏。在系统级物料清单上，Intel也进行了全面优化：集成Wi-Fi 7和USB PD控制器以减少OEM额外采购成本，采用更窄的内存总线和6层PCB（而非常见的8层）来降低整体成本。项目Firefly计划则进一步利用移动供应链来降低预算级笔记本的制造成本。值得注意的是，有一个组件反而增加了成本——为LPE簇提供专用电源轨。这个被称为“低功耗岛”的LPE簇在Wildcat Lake中至关重要，因为所有SKU仅配备1到2个P-core，专用电源轨让绝大多数轻负载任务在LPE簇上运行，从而大幅延长电池续航。

Wildcat Lake是近年来消费级芯片领域最有趣的产品之一，它打破了预算芯片必然采用落后工艺和旧架构的惯例，以最新制程和开放的UCIe标准实现了成本与性能的巧妙平衡，因此荣获Tom's Hardware 2026年度创新奖。

items.title: Hot Chips 2026: Intel dives deep on Crescent Island AI accelerator — larger caches and deeper XMX engines target maximum AI FLOPS per watt
items.description: At Hot Chips 2026, Intel detailed more about its Crescent Island AI accelerator, which uses the Xe3P architecture. The accelerator will use liquid-cooled chips and HBM4 memory to serve inference workloads in data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter This Tom's Hardware Premium article is free to read with a Tom's Hardware account; no payment necessary. We're offering free access from August 23 to 26 so you can read all of our reporting from Hot Chips.Intel shared more details of its Crescent Island AI accelerator, powered by the Xe3P architecture, at the Hot Chips symposium this week. Unlike Nvidia's Rubin and AMD's MI455X GPUs, which are high-power, exclusively liquid-cooled chips with massive pools of HBM4 memory that provide maximum performance across both AI training and inference workloads, Crescent Island is designed to fit into a lower-power, inference-first niche in the AI accelerator market. (Image credit: Intel)As a refresher, Crescent Island is a 350W air-cooled PCIe card that uses up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory, meaning it can be deployed in traditional servers without exotic power and cooling requirements. We've already learned about some of Crescent Island's DNA from past disclosures, but Intel went deeper into the chip's architectural details at Hot Chips.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Intel)Crescent Island is built up from four Xe3P slices, each containing eight Xe Cores, for a total of 32. Each Xe Core has eight Xe Vector Engines and eight XMX matrix accelerators, for a total of 256 of each resource.The Xe3 graphics architecture, as seen on Intel's Panther Lake processors, already modified the capacity and flexibility of the GPU cache hierarchy to improve utilization and decrease performance-sapping register spills, and Xe3P further refines that hierarchy. You may like Intel details long-awaited Crescent Island AI GPU at Computex, boasts up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X to combat memory shortages Hot Chips 2026: Intel Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' comes with up to 256 P-cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache Nvidia deep dives Vera CPU for AI data centers (Image credit: Intel)The Xe3P Xe Core has twice the amount of general register file space for working data versus Battlemage. Each Xe Core now has 1MB of general-purpose register file space, up from 512KB on Battlemage and Xe2. In addition, Xe3P offers 512KB of L1 cache or shared local memory per Xe Core, a structure that started out at 256KB on Battlemage and grew by approximately 1.33x on Panther Lake's Xe3 GPU. The chip also has 32MB of shared L2 cache. These expanded caches are meant to serve the chip's larger matrix accelerators on its AI compute-focused mission.Xe3P boasts a larger systolic depth in its XMX engines than past Xe GPU designs. Xe3P's XMX systolic engines are a 16-deep design, meaning they can process matrices in much larger chunks than the four-deep systolic design of Xe2 and Xe3. Nvidia doesn't discuss the architecture of its Tensor Cores in anywhere near this level of detail, but as an AI inference-focused part, the fact that Xe3P can theoretically work on more elements at once during general matrix-multiply operations is an important capability boost for Crescent Island's inference ambitions.Intel is also prioritizing a broad range of data types with this chip, from FP4 formats with microscaling support (aka MXFP4) all the way to what it describes as full-rate double-precision (via 64 FP64 FMA units per Xe Core). FP64 isn't widely used in AI workloads, but Intel says that the inclusion of full-rate processing for that data type makes Crescent Island useful as a converged high-performance computing and AI chip. (Image credit: Intel)Each Xe Core also supports sigmoid and tanh transcendental functions, which are important to a variety of operations during AI inference, especially the softmax function. AMD and Nvidia have prioritized the performance of these functions in their recent architectures as well, so the fact that Xe3P offers support for them is key for its AI-first initiatives.While Crescent Island does have a media codec block featuring four encoders and decoders to help serve up video to multimodal AI models, gamers hoping for a glimpse of future Arc cards won’t find it with this product, as graphics-specific functionality like RT cores has been omitted from this chip to preserve die area for compute functionality. What to read next Hot Chips 2026: Intel details cutting-edge tech in entry-level Wildcat Lake Google reportedly books Intel for packaging more than 3 million TPUs in 2028 AMD takes the wraps off its Instinct MI455X AI accelerator (Image credit: Intel)As a data-center-focused part, Crescent Island offers a full suite of reliability, availability, and serviceability features, including ECC and parity protection across the die and a range of memory reliability features. (Image credit: Intel)As for the specific applications that Crescent Island will target, Intel highlights the rise of mixture-of-experts models paired with speculative decoding as a new class of workload that Crescent Island can serve well.Speculative decoding strategies vary, but in general, they use a fast, lightweight mechanism to create drafts of future tokens that the main model can then be used to accept or reject, potentially improving decode performance. Not every draft token generated this way will be approved, but much like speculative execution in CPUs, it helps produce useful work from compute resources that would otherwise be left idle.As model serving recipes pursue more aggressive drafting mechanisms, more compute is required to generate those draft tokens. At a high level, that understanding changes the common perception of decode as being a mostly memory-bandwidth-bound operation.As an LPDDR5X-powered chip, Crescent Island won't have the eye-popping bandwidth of HBM-backed accelerators at its disposal for maximum performance with traditional autoregressive decode, so any help it can get from these speculative methods will be helpful.Overall, Intel claims that Crescent Island is built to offer high FLOPS per watt and that it's optimized for compute-bound workloads like prefill (aka prompt processing and KV cache construction). Intel's emphasis on those areas of AI performance, as well as heterogeneous deployments, suggests that this chip could have a niche alongside HBM-backed accelerators whose resources are best used for decode operations.Intel and its partner SambaNova could both stand to benefit from such an arrangement, as that company's SN50 inference accelerators are explicitly built to benefit from disaggregated prefill processing powered by GPUs. SN50 racks and Crescent Island are both meant to serve as lower-power, air-cooled systems that customers can deploy in existing data centers without dramatic upgrades to power or cooling infrastructure, so there is broad synergy in the shape of those products.Intel still isn't discussing just how many theoretical compute FLOPS to expect from Crescent Island, nor is it disclosing memory bandwidth figures. But the architectural decisions it's shared so far — getting lots of data close to the compute engines of the chip and processing more of it at once in a relatively narrow power envelope — seem sound in a world where the company is still trying to reset its AI ambitions after a string of high-profile product failures and cancellations.Intel has promised Crescent Island for a second-half 2026 time frame, and the clock is ticking on that launch window, so we’re eager to learn more about the chip’s final specifications, as well as customer and partner wins, when that launch does occur. items.titleZh: Hot Chips 2026: Intel dives deep on Crescent Island AI accelerator — larger caches and deeper XMX engines target maximum AI FLOPS per watt
items.descriptionZh:
在Hot Chips 2026研讨会上，英特尔进一步披露了其面向AI推理加速的Crescent Island芯片架构细节。这款产品基于全新的Xe3P架构，与英伟达Rubin和AMD MI455X等采用超大容量HBM4内存、功耗极高且必须液冷、面向训练与推理双场景的旗舰GPU不同，Crescent Island瞄准的是低功耗、风冷、以推理优先的细分市场。它是一张350W功耗的PCIe卡，支持最高480GB LPDDR5X内存，无需特殊供电和液冷即可部署在传统服务器中，大幅降低了AI加速的落地门槛。

从芯片内部结构来看，Crescent Island由四个Xe3P切片组成，每个切片包含8个Xe核心，总计32个Xe核心。每个Xe核心内部有8个Xe向量引擎和8个XMX矩阵加速单元，整颗芯片共提供256个向量引擎和256个矩阵加速单元。Xe3P架构在缓存层次上做了显著增强：每个Xe核心的通用寄存器文件（GRF）容量从Battlemage（Xe2）的512KB翻倍至1MB，用于存放工作数据；每个Xe核心的L1缓存/共享本地内存从Battlemage的256KB提升到512KB，相比Panther Lake上Xe3的约1.33倍增长再次扩大；此外芯片还配备32MB共享L2缓存。这些大容量缓存设计旨在为更大的矩阵运算单元提供充足的数据供给，减少寄存器溢出带来的性能损失。

Xe3P的XMX矩阵引擎还采用了16级脉动阵列（systolic array）设计，而Xe2和Xe3的脉动深度仅为4级。这意味着在通用矩阵乘法运算中，Crescent Island理论上可以一次性处理更大规模的数据块，对推理性能提升至关重要。在数据类型支持上，该芯片覆盖从支持微缩格式的FP4（MXFP4）到全速双精度（每个Xe核心集成64个FP64 FMA单元）的广泛范围。尽管FP64在AI工作负载中并不常用，但英特尔的这一设计使Crescent Island能够兼顾高性能计算（HPC）与AI推理，成为融合型算力芯片。每个Xe核心还支持sigmoid和tanh超越函数，这对AI推理中的softmax操作等关键环节非常重要，AMD和英伟达近年也在各自架构中重点优化了此类函数的执行效率。

值得一提的是，Crescent Island虽然集成了包含4个编码器和4个解码器的媒体编解码模块，用于为多模态AI模型提供视频输入支持，但它完全移除了图形专用功能（如光线追踪核心），以节省芯片面积用于计算单元。因此这款产品不会直接预示未来Arc显卡的设计方向。作为数据中心级芯片，它还提供了完整的可靠性、可用性和可维护性（RAS）特性，包括全芯片ECC和奇偶校验保护，以及多种内存可靠性机制。

在应用场景上，英特尔特别强调了混合专家（MoE）模型与推测解码（speculative decoding）相结合的新兴工作负载。推测解码通常使用一个轻量快速的机制预先生成候选token，再由主模型接受或拒绝，从而在推理解码阶段提升性能——虽然并非每个草稿token都会被采纳，但类似于CPU中的推测执行，它能让原本闲置的计算资源产生有效工作。随着服务端采用更激进的草稿生成策略，生成草稿token所需的计算量也在增加，这使得解码过程不再仅仅是内存带宽受限的操作，而更加依赖算力。由于Crescent Island采用LPDDR5X内存，其带宽无法与HBM加速器相比，因此推测解码带来的计算效率提升对其尤为重要。

总体而言，英特尔将Crescent Island定位为一款高每瓦FLOPS的加速器，专门优化了计算密集型工作负载，如预填充（prefill，即提示词处理和KV缓存构建）阶段。这种对异构部署的强调，使它有望与HBM加速器形成互补：HBM加速器资源更适合解码阶段，而Crescent Island可以承担预填充等计算密集任务。英特尔与其合作伙伴SambaNova都可能从这种分工中获益——SambaNova的SN50推理加速器正是为利用GPU驱动的分离式预填充处理而设计的，且SN50机架和Crescent Island都面向低功耗、风冷、可部署于现有数据中心的产品形态，两者在业务定位上高度协同。

英特尔尚未公布Crescent Island的具体理论算力（FLOPS）和内存带宽数据，但从已披露的架构决策来看——让大量数据贴近计算引擎，并在相对紧凑的功耗范围内一次性处理更多数据——这些方向在当前英特尔经历一系列AI产品挫折后试图重振雄风的背景下显得颇为合理。英特尔承诺Crescent Island将在2026年下半年推出，时间窗口正在逼近，届时我们有望获知最终规格及客户与合作伙伴的采用情况。

items.content: OpenAI says its new AI chip, Jalapeño, completes tasks more efficiently and returns responses faster than other AI systems, according to a blog post published on Tuesday. During a briefing with reporters, OpenAI hardware vice president Richard Ho said Jalapeño offers the “best of both worlds” with lower latency and higher throughput, as AI systems typically “have to make a trade-off between the two.”First introduced in June, Jalapeño is an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) made in partnership with Broadcom. It’s designed for AI inference — the process of running a trained AI model to complete a task or deploy an agent.This chart measures Jalapeño’s time between tokens (TBT) — or the time it takes to deliver a response. Image: OpenAITo measure Jalapeño’s performance, OpenAI used InferenceX, a benchmarking platform that shows how well AI systems handle inference. The test compared Jalapeño’s performance against the best results recorded at the time, which were with Nvidia’s GB200 or GB300 superchips. OpenAI says Jalapeño delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1, and Kimi K2.5 1T than the comparison systems, while offering 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency across the three models. That means the chip can provide users with “faster responses, more responsive agents, and more reliable access as the demand grows,” according to Ho.Jalapeño can perform more work while using less energy, according to OpenAI. Image: OpenAIOpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño in “small volumes” by the end of this year, but will begin to “ramp the volume up” into 2027, Ho added. The company doesn’t say how many chips it plans to deploy next year, however.Even with these performance improvements, Ho said OpenAI doesn’t expect to replace its entire chip lineup with Jalapeño, saying its overall compute strategy includes “very good partners,” like Nvidia. OpenAI will continue developing the second and third generations of the new chip.

items.titleZh: OpenAI称其Jalapeño芯片能比竞争对手提供更快的AI响应
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI于周二发布博客文章，宣布其自研AI芯片“Jalapeño”在执行任务时比现有AI系统效率更高、响应速度更快。OpenAI硬件副总裁Richard Ho在记者会上表示，Jalapeño实现了“两全其美”——既降低了延迟，又提高了吞吐量，而传统AI系统通常被迫在这两者之间做出取舍。

Jalapeño芯片于今年6月首次亮相，是由OpenAI与博通合作设计的专用集成电路（ASIC），专为AI推理而打造。所谓AI推理，是指利用已经训练好的模型来执行具体任务或部署智能体的过程，与训练阶段相比，推理对算力和能效的要求截然不同。ASIC正是针对这类特定工作负载进行定制优化的芯片，相比通用GPU在执行固定任务时往往更具能效优势。

为了验证性能，OpenAI使用了自研的InferenceX基准测试平台，评估不同AI系统处理推理任务的能力。测试将Jalapeño与当时表现最优异的Nvidia GB200或GB300超级芯片进行对比，覆盖GPT-OSS 120B、DeepSeek R1和Kimi K2.5 1T三个大型模型。结果显示，Jalapeño在每瓦特性能上比对比系统高出1.5至1.9倍，同时端到端延迟降低了1.7至3.6倍。这意味着在实际使用中，Jalapeño能够以更低能耗完成更多计算任务，并显著缩短从请求到生成回复的时间。OpenAI还通过“token间延迟”（TBT）——即生成回复时相邻token之间的间隔时间——来直观展示该芯片的响应速度优势。

Ho指出，得益于这些改进，Jalapeño能为用户带来“更快的响应、更灵敏的智能体，以及在高需求下更稳定的访问体验”。部署方面，OpenAI计划于今年年底先以“小规模”应用Jalapeño，随后到2027年逐步扩大产量，但官方并未透露明年的具体部署数量。

尽管Jalapeño在推理任务上表现出色，Ho强调OpenAI不会用它完全替换现有芯片阵容。公司的整体算力策略仍会与包括Nvidia在内的“优秀合作伙伴”保持紧密协作，同时OpenAI也将继续推进Jalapeño第二代和第三代芯片的研发工作。这说明OpenAI希望通过多元化的硬件组合来优化成本、性能与供应弹性，而非单纯依赖某一家供应商或自研芯片。

items.title: China strategically slows exports of critical materials used in semiconductor fabrication to Taiwan — germanium and quartz exports to the region also threaten optical and robotics supply chain
items.description: China slows exports of germanium, quartz-based materials, and magnets. The move potentially disrupts the optical connectivity, semiconductor, and robotics industries.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China is slowing or restricting shipments of materials based on germanium and quartz to Taiwan, which creates supply constraints for multiple industries on the island, according to Nikkei. Companies are reporting problems obtaining germanium- and quartz-based materials as well as permanent magnets from Chinese suppliers as customs procedures extend delivery times. In some cases, Taiwanese manufacturers lose orders while waiting for clearance.China imposed export controls on germanium in 2023 and on quartz (SiO2) in late 2024. At one point, China even restricted exports of gallium and germanium to the U.S., but later lifted the ban and imposed an export control regime. Under the regime, the exporter must disclose the customer and intended use by the end user, which enables Chinese authorities to essentially view, and to some degree, control the whole supply chain. China's Ministry of Commerce can approve, reject, or effectively delay the shipment while reviewing it, which is apparently what it does these days.The Nikkei story strongly suggests that the delays are selective rather than a blanket slowdown of all germanium, quartz, and magnet exports to Taiwan. Germanium, quartz, and magnets can be used widely across many industries. Yet, the report specifically pins germanium and quartz to optics/photonics and semiconductor manufacturing, and permanent neodymium magnets to the aerospace industry that produces high-performance motors for robotics.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While the report does not determine exactly how granular the targeting is, Nikkei's sources specifically come from optical technology, semiconductor equipment, and aerospace companies. Another thing to note is that all of Nikkei's sources come from Taiwan, indicating that China targets select verticals of the island, not the same verticals globally.In general, the situation looks less like 'no germanium/quartz/magnets for Taiwan' and more like selective friction applied through China's dual-use export-control regime. The particularly interesting part is that Beijing may not need a Taiwan-specific embargo: by examining the material, buyer, end user, and shipment, authorities can potentially slow strategically sensitive supply chains (think optical connectivity for data centers) while allowing less sensitive trade to continue. You may like Ajinomoto reportedly cuts critical chip packaging film supply to China by 30% as domestic substitutes race to qualify How optical interconnects and silicon photonics emerged as AI's next hot commodity While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market GermaniumGermanium is widely used in infrared optics (Ge), silicon photonics (Ge), photodetectors (Ge), and optical fiber (GeO2). China controls about 63% of the global germanium — both elemental and dioxide — supply, whereas all other countries — led by Belgium, Canada, and Japan — control 37% of the market, according to InvestInGermanium.com. The U.S. mostly gets germanium and germanium dioxide from Belgium and Canada, according to Introl.com. Meanwhile, Belgium and Japan also import germanium from China, which highlights that the world still largely depends on China when it comes to germanium supply.While infrared optics is certainly a concern for state security as it is used for night-vision equipment, aerospace sensors, and military systems, it looks like China is more concerned about optical connectivity that is crucial for AI data centers.In silicon photonics, germanium is mainly used to make photodetectors. Silicon cannot efficiently detect light at the ~1.3 µm and 1.55 µm wavelengths commonly used for optical communications, but germanium can. By integrating germanium with silicon waveguides, manufacturers can build high-speed Ge-on-Si photodiodes that convert optical signals into electrical ones. These detectors are used in optical transceivers and data-center interconnects and could play an important role in co-packaged optics (CPO).Equally important, germanium dioxide is crucial for optical fiber manufacturing. Adding GeO₂ to silica raises its refractive index and enables manufacturers to form a higher-index fiber core surrounded by lower-index silica cladding in a bid to confine light inside the fiber. Germanium doping also increases silica's photosensitivity, which enables fabrication of fiber Bragg gratings used for wavelength filtering, optical communications, lasers, and sensing.China's dominant position in germanium gives the country potential leverage over multiple layers of the optical connectivity supply chain, from silicon photonics photodetectors all the way to the optical fiber itself. If restrictions cover the appropriate germanium products and persist long enough, they could increase lead times and constrain production across several optical-interconnect segments simultaneously. What to read next Taiwan weighs criminal ban on AI chip exports to all of China FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers China is considering export controls on AI technologies, including banning local companies from using TSMC, report claims However, none of the optical connectivity applications depend exclusively on China. Germanium can come from non-Chinese producers, recycling, inventories, and alternative supply chains, and not every optical fiber necessarily has the same germanium requirements. In fact, the refractive-index difference can also be engineered with other dopants, eliminating the need for germanium or its dioxide completely. Furthermore, the report states that China is slowing clearances for Taiwanese companies, which does not automatically mean it is slowing down clearances for companies based in other countries. Of course, increasing the lead times for Taiwan-based companies can impact multiple optical initiatives, though the actual effect remains to be seen.QuartzChina produces large volumes of silica sands and quartz sands for glass, construction, fiber optics, semiconductors, and other industrial uses. Quartz (SiO2) is used very widely in the semiconductor industry both as a component of chipmaking tools and as the base for silicon wafers. Meanwhile, the Nikkei report does not give enough technical specifications of SiO2 to determine which applications the restrictions target.It should be noted that semiconductor wafers require high-purity quartz with no impurities (≥99.99% SiO2), and China is not the leading producer of HPQ, so it can hardly use its exports as leverage. This potentially brings us back to the optical connectivity market.High-purity fused silica (SiO₂), produced from quartz or synthetic silica feedstocks, is the primary glass material used to make most optical fibers as it combines very low optical loss at telecom wavelengths with excellent thermal and mechanical stability as well as chemical resistance. Both the fiber core and cladding are typically silica-based, but their refractive indices are deliberately made slightly different to keep light confined inside the core. A common approach is to dope the SiO2 core with germanium dioxide (GeO2) to raise its refractive index, while the surrounding cladding remains mostly SiO2 with a lower refractive index.Meanwhile, optical fiber is commonly produced from synthetic ultra-high-purity silica, not from natural crystalline quartz. Manufacturers typically create the fiber preform by chemical vapor deposition using precursors such as SiCl4, which is oxidized to form extremely pure SiO2. Then, dopants like GeO2 can be used to modify the core's refractive index.That said, China's quartz restrictions can disrupt parts of the optical-component supply chain, but the Nikkei report does not demonstrate that they threaten optical fiber production itself. In fact, germanium/GeO2 restrictions could be a more direct concern for Ge-doped fiber cores than quartz in general.NeodymiumWhile China holds a dominant share of the neodymium production, it does not export control the rare earth material itself, as its real leverage is in processing and refining. NdFeB (neodymium-iron-boron) permanent magnets are used in a wide range of applications, but high-performance grades for aerospace and robotics often contain terbium or dysprosium to increase coercivity and maintain their magnetic properties at high temperatures. China's export controls do not limit neodymium itself or permanent magnets, but NdFeB permanent magnets or magnetic powders containing terbium or dysprosium.While permanent magnets can be used in HDDs as well as various pumps or motors used in data centers, these applications do not need permanent magnets containing terbium or dysprosium, so it doesn't seem this regulation has anything to do with AI data centers. Yet, it has a lot to do with emerging applications in the aerospace and robotics realms, so slowing down rivals helps China to establish or maintain its lead, as finding cost-effective alternatives to Chinese permanent magnets is not an easy task. Then again, the report only covers companies from Taiwan, and we have no idea how it impacts companies based elsewhere.A potential play for leverageRather than imposing a blanket ban, Beijing appears to be using its dual-use export-control regime to selectively delay shipments based on materials, customers, and end uses to gain leverage over strategically important industries. The biggest potential impact could be on optical connectivity, where China's dominance in germanium supply gives it influence over both silicon-photonics photodetectors and Ge-doped optical fiber.However, while the effect of the curbs on Taiwanese industries may be significant, what remains unclear is the impact of China's restrictions on the global market.

items.descriptionZh:
中国正在通过出口管制机制，对运往台湾的锗、石英（二氧化硅）及稀土永磁体等材料实施选择性延迟放行。据《日经新闻》报道，多家台湾企业反映，从中国供应商处获取锗基材料、石英基材料及钕铁硼永磁体时遭遇清关时间大幅延长，部分厂商甚至因等待许可而丢失订单。这一做法并非全面禁止，而是针对特定行业和最终用途的“精准摩擦”，意在保持中国在关键供应链上的战略杠杆。

### 背景：从出口管制到选择性延迟

中国于2023年对锗实施出口管制，2024年底又将石英（SiO2）纳入管制清单。此前，中国曾一度限制对美出口镓和锗，随后取消禁令并转为实施出口管制制度。根据现行制度，出口商必须申报最终客户和用途，使中国商务部能够审查乃至掌控整个供应链——它有权批准、拒绝或通过延长审查时间实质搁置货物。日经新闻报道显示，当前这些延迟明显具有选择性，而非对所有锗、石英和磁铁出口一视同仁。虽然这些材料广泛应用于多个行业，但报道特别指出，锗和石英主要关联光学/光子学与半导体制造，而含铽或镝的高性能钕铁硼永磁体则关联航空航天及机器人领域。消息源均来自台湾的光学技术、半导体设备与航空航天企业，暗示中国针对的是台湾的特定垂直行业，而非全球同类行业。

### 锗：光互连供应链的命脉

锗在战略产业中地位特殊，主要应用于红外光学（夜视设备、航空航天传感器、军事系统）、硅光子学、光电探测器和光纤制造。中国控制着全球约63%的锗（含单质和二氧化物）供应，其余37%由比利时、加拿大、日本等国掌控。美国主要从比利时和加拿大进口，但比利时和日本同样从中国进口锗——这凸显了世界对中国的深度依赖。

在硅光子学领域，锗的核心作用在于制造光电探测器。硅无法高效探测光通信常用的1.3微米和1.55微米波段光信号，而锗具备这一能力。通过将锗与硅波导集成，可制造高速锗硅（Ge-on-Si）光电二极管，把光信号转换为电信号。这些探测器广泛用于光收发器和数据中心互连，并有望在共封装光学（CPO）中扮演关键角色。此外，二氧化锗（GeO₂）是光纤制造的关键掺杂剂：向二氧化硅中加入GeO₂可提高纤芯折射率，形成折射率较高的纤芯与折射率较低的包层，从而将光限制在光纤内传播；锗掺杂还能增强二氧化硅的光敏性，用于制造光纤布拉格光栅，服务于波长滤波、光通信、激光和传感等应用。

由于中国在锗供应中的主导地位，北京对光互连供应链拥有多层施压能力——从硅光子探测器到光纤本身。若限制措施覆盖合适的锗产品并持续足够长，可能同时拉长多个光互连领域的交货周期并抑制产能。但文章也指出，光互连应用并非绝对依赖中国：锗可从非中国产地、回收、库存和替代渠道获取；光纤折射率差也可通过其他掺杂剂实现，完全不需要锗或GeO₂。此外，放缓清关仅针对台湾企业，其他国家企业未必受影响，实际冲击尚待观察。

### 石英：更多影响组件，而非光纤制造

中国生产大量硅砂和石英砂，用于玻璃、建筑、光纤、半导体等行业。石英在半导体产业中用途广泛，既是芯片制造设备的部件，也是硅晶圆的基底材料。但日经报道未提供SiO2的具体技术规格，难以判断限制目标。

值得注意的是，半导体晶圆要求极高纯度的石英（≥99.99% SiO2），而中国并非高纯石英（HPQ）的主要生产国，难以在此领域形成有效杠杆。因此，石英管制的矛头更可能指向光学连接领域。高纯度熔融石英（SiO2）是制造大多数光纤的主要玻璃材料，具有极低的光学损耗、优异的热稳定性和化学稳定性。但现代光纤通常使用合成超高纯石英，而非天然水晶——制造者以四氯化硅（SiCl4）等前体通过化学气相沉积氧化生成极纯的SiO2，再用GeO2等掺杂剂调节纤芯折射率。因此，中国石英限制可能扰乱部分光学组件供应链，但报道并未证明其会直接威胁光纤生产本身。相比之下，锗/GeO2限制对掺锗光纤纤芯的威胁更为直接。

### 钕磁铁：精准打击航空航天与机器人

中国在钕生产领域占据主导份额，但出口管制的真正抓手是后端的加工和精炼。钕铁硼（NdFeB）永磁体应用广泛，但高性能等级（用于航空航天和机器人）通常添加铽或镝以提高矫顽力，从而在高温下保持磁性能。中国的出口管制并不限制钕本身或普通永磁体，而是针对含有铽或镝的NdFeB永磁体及磁粉。

尽管永磁体可用于硬盘驱动器或数据中心的各种泵和电机，但这些应用并不需要含铽/镝的高性能磁体，因此该规定与AI数据中心无关。其真正目标指向航空航天和机器人新兴领域——通过延缓竞争对手，中国可巩固或扩大自身领先优势，因为要找到替代中国永磁体的经济方案并非易事。不过，报道仅涉及台湾企业，对其他国家企业的影响尚不明确。

### 总结：战略性摩擦，而非全面禁运

总体来看，中国并非对台湾实施锗、石英、磁铁的“一刀切”禁运，而是通过两用出口管制制度，针对材料、客户和最终用途进行选择性延迟，借此对战略敏感供应链（如数据中心光连接）施加压力，同时允许非敏感贸易正常进行。最大的潜在影响集中在光互连领域——中国凭借锗供应优势，既影响硅光子光电探测器，也影响掺锗光纤。然而，尽管对台湾相关产业的影响可能显著，这些限制对全球市场的实际冲击仍有待持续观察。

items.title: Nvidia Jetson Orin-guided Russian AI drone killed three civilians in Ukraine, forensic teams say — first documented case of civilian deaths caused by a Russian drone using fully autonomous targeting
items.description: A Russian Molniya drone carrying an Nvidia Jetson Orin module killed three civilians at a gas station in Zaporizhzhia last month.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A Russian Molniya drone carrying an Nvidia Jetson Orin module crashed and killed three civilians at a gas station in Zaporizhzhia last month after choosing its final target without a human pilot, according to a New York Times investigation that cites Ukrainian air defense commanders, drone experts, and the forensic team that examined the wreckage.Kateryna Bondar, a senior fellow at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told the paper it's the first documented case of civilian deaths caused by a Russian drone using fully autonomous targeting. The dead were Tetiana Bubynets, a 19-year-old accounting student, and two men aged 41 and 48.Human operators launched the drone toward the gas station, per the report, but the final aim point was selected onboard by software trained to recognize objects such as propane tanks. The aircraft failed to clear an apartment building on its approach, struck a wall, and detonated near people sheltering below, rather than striking its chosen target.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The strike drone flew in a group of roughly half a dozen aircraft, none of which emitted radio traffic, Ukrainian air defense officials said. Modules recovered from this attack and from intact test drones carried no encryption, so investigators could examine both the terrain imagery loaded for visual navigation and the code specifying which object classes the drone had been trained to attack. "Machines are making decisions to strike," Col. Serhiy Minaiev, Zaporizhzhia's air defense commander, told the NYT. Russia is understood to have begun AI-guided test flights of the mass-produced, fixed-wing Molniya in May, after months of self-targeting trials with the V2U.Nvidia confirmed to the New York Times that modules photographed in the recovered drones were Jetson Orin minicomputers, hardware that sells for a few hundred dollars. "Our Jetson Orin modules are consumer-grade products sold to students, developers, and startups for a wide range of beneficial applications," an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. "They are not available in Russia and are not designed for military purposes. Pre-owned Jetsons are available through many reseller channels. Although we cannot track products after they are sold, if we determine that any customer is violating U.S. export controls, we will take appropriate action." You may like Ukraine used 10 AI-controlled ‘Terminator’ drones to kill Russian soldiers two years ago, marking first autonomous killings of humans Nvidia Jetson chip found in Russian cruise missile, Ukraine claims Ukraine built a $48,000 long-range drone after covertly snapping Chinese factory photos Ukrainian investigators have now linked the Jetson Orin to four Russian weapon families. A teardown by Ukraine's GUR intelligence agency last June found one seated on a Chinese Leetop A603 carrier board inside the V2U loitering munition, in combat use since February 2025. Weeks later, a Ukrainian general said the module powered object recognition in the upgraded Shahed MS001, and earlier this month Ukraine reported the same silicon in the S-71M Monochrome cruise missile. Data-center AI accelerators fall under U.S. export controls; edge modules like the Jetson Orin, with variants starting at $249, don't.Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's recently ousted defense minister, told the NYT that Kyiv tested its own fully autonomous system against fuel storage and military equipment in occupied Crimea in recent months, and Ukrainian quadcopters killed Russian soldiers in autonomous mode as far back as 2024. In Zaporizhzhia, defenses now include roughly 240 miles of anti-drone netting and plastic sheeting propped at odd angles around propane tanks to throw off image recognition.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.descriptionZh:
一架搭载英伟达（Nvidia）Jetson Orin模块的俄罗斯"莫尔尼亚"（Molniya）自杀式无人机，在上月对扎波罗热州一处加油站的袭击中，在无人飞行员介入的情况下自主选择了最终攻击目标，最终导致三名平民死亡。据《纽约时报》援引乌克兰防空指挥官、无人机专家及对残骸进行取证的团队调查显示，这是有记录以来首个由俄军无人机完全自主瞄准并造成平民死亡的案例。三名遇难者分别是19岁的会计学学生Tetiana Bubynets，以及两名分别为41岁和48岁的男子。

报道称，操作员发射了无人机并引导其飞向加油站方向，但最终瞄准点由机载软件自主决定——该软件经过训练，能够识别丙烷气罐等物体特征。然而，无人机在接近目标时未能飞越一栋公寓楼，撞上墙壁后在楼下躲避人群附近爆炸，未能击中预定目标。乌克兰防空官员透露，参与此次袭击的约六架无人机编队均未发射任何无线电信号。从袭击现场及缴获的完好测试无人机中回收的模块没有加密，调查人员因此可以检视用于视觉导航的地形影像，以及规定无人机攻击对象类别的代码。扎波罗热防空指挥官Serhiy Minaiev上校向《纽约时报》表示："是机器在做开火的决策。"据悉，俄罗斯自5月起就开始对量产的固定翼"莫尔尼亚"无人机进行AI引导试飞，此前已用V2U型号进行了数月的自主瞄准试验。

英伟达向《纽约时报》确认，回收无人机中拍到的模块是Jetson Orin迷你计算机，该硬件售价仅为数百美元。英伟达发言人向Tom's Hardware表示："我们的Jetson Orin模块是面向学生、开发者和初创公司的消费级产品，用于广泛的正当应用。它们不在俄罗斯销售，也并非为军事用途设计。二手Jetson产品可通过多种经销商渠道获得。虽然我们无法追踪已售出的产品，但如果我们认定任何客户违反美国出口管制，将采取适当行动。"

乌克兰调查人员现已将Jetson Orin与四种俄制武器型号建立关联。乌克兰国防部情报总局（GUR）去年6月的拆解分析显示，V2U巡飞弹中（自2025年2月起投入实战）搭载了一颗安装在中国Leetop A603载板上的Jetson Orin模块。数周后，乌克兰一名将军透露该模块为升级版"沙赫德"（Shahed）MS001无人机提供目标识别能力；本月早些时候，乌克兰报告称S-71M Monochrome巡航导弹中也发现了同样的芯片。值得注意的是，数据中心AI加速器受美国出口管制，而Jetson Orin这类边缘计算模块（起售价249美元）不受管制。

乌克兰最近被撤职的国防部长Mykhailo Fedorov向《纽约时报》表示，基辅方面近几个月也在被占领的克里米亚对燃料库和军事装备测试了自己的完全自主攻击系统，且乌克兰四轴无人机早在2024年就曾以自主模式击杀俄军士兵。在扎波罗热，防御措施现已包括约240英里（约386公里）的反无人机网，以及在丙烷罐周围以不同角度架设塑料布，以干扰图像识别系统。

items.title: Hot Chips 2026: Micron warns HBM wafer penalty is widening with every generation — AI memory uses 3x more silicon than DDR5, company says memory wall is 'getting worse' as prices rise
items.description: Micron Fellow Raghu Sreeramaneni told the Hot Chips 2026 conference that the silicon penalty HBM carries against DDR5 is growing with every generation.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter This Tom's Hardware Premium article is free to read with a Tom's Hardware account; no payment necessary. We're offering free access from August 23 to 26 so you can read all of our reporting from Hot Chips.Raghu Sreeramaneni, Micron HBM Design Architecture Fellow, told the Hot Chips 2026 conference on August 23 that the silicon penalty HBM carries against DDR5 is growing with every generation, and that it can’t be closed without giving up performance, something that Micron won’t do. Pressed on whether newer parts narrow the gap, he said it’s "definitely not getting better," putting the current overhead at roughly three times the wafer area of DDR5 for the same capacity. That trajectory is the reason why PC memory hit record prices this year, with conventional DRAM contract prices up 90% to 95% quarter over quarter in the first quarter of 2026. (Image credit: Micron)Wafer mathematicsAn HBM4 die fits 256 banks against 32 on a DDR5 die, and it reaches its bandwidth by running those banks in parallel, which requires far more die area for data paths, power delivery, and the through-silicon vias (TSVs) that link each layer to the base die. A single HBM3E die can feed 256 GB/s, while one DDR5 die supplies about 8 GB/s, so matching a given bit count makes the HBM die much larger.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Micron has publicly put that overhead at about three times the wafer area of DDR5, and Sreeramaneni said it traces to an HBM3E-against-DDR5 comparison that grows with each generation as pin speeds, bank counts, stack heights, and die sizes climb higher. He called HBM "probably the most cross-functionally complex solution that we make," and noted that in a two-GPU package, memory accounts for around 90% of the silicon, roughly eight times the area of the GPU dies. HBM already sells for about five times the price of DDR5 per bit, so each wafer a maker moves to it removes a disproportionate share of commodity memory from the market, pushing consumer product prices higher as a consequence. (Image credit: Micron)Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90% to 95% quarter over quarter in the first quarter of 2026 and a further 58% to 63% in the second. To put that into perspective, a mainstream 32GB DDR5-6000 kit sold for around $392 this month, up from $110 to $140 a year earlier, and 128GB of DDR5 passed $3,399, a 500% rise over 12 months, with European prices up 345% since September last year. Back in February, HP told investors that DRAM now makes up 35% of its PC build cost, up from 15% to 18% a quarter earlier, and Gartner expects PC shipments to fall more than 10% in 2026. While it’s true that the surge eased to 13% to 18% in the third quarter, that happened because consumer electronics makers reached the ceiling of what they could pass on, not because supply improved. You may like Hot Chips 2026: SK hynix pushes hybrid bonding to HBM5 as AI memory hits 775-micron ceiling Researchers turn HBM on its side to tackle AI memory’s heat wall The rise of local agentic computing faces a brutal reality: rising DRAM prices Bandwidth, stacking, and heatMicron's presentation put compute performance scaling at roughly three times every two years and HBM bandwidth at under two times, a divergence Sreeramaneni summarized by saying "the memory wall is still present, and, in fact, maybe getting worse." HBM4 doubles the host interface to 2,048 I/Os, and Micron's parts run above 11 Gb/s per pin for more than 2.8 TB/s per stack, beyond the 8 Gb/s and 2 TB/s baseline in JEDEC's HBM4 standard.Each of those gains comes from more parallelism, which enlarges the die again and widens the silicon ratio. Sreeramaneni said there is "a good path to 16 layers of DRAM," but "after 16, there's still a lot of work to be done." Meanwhile, SK hynix used its own Hot Chips talk to describe a 775-micron total-thickness ceiling that caps stacking until the industry adopts hybrid bonding, which SK hynix doesn't expect before HBM5. Micron's HBM4E, due around 2027, moves the logic base die to a TSMC foundry process, part of a wider shift toward customization as AI workloads fragment, which Sreeramaneni described by saying "disaggregation is the buzzword now." (Image credit: Micron)The base die runs hottest because it sits at the bottom of the stack, doing the highest-speed interface work while the heatsink sits at the top. Every layer added between the base and the heatsink then raises thermal resistance. Sreeramaneni said Micron is now "architecting solutions around thermals rather than the other way around," a reversal from a few years ago. Micron highlighted how Meta's Llama 3 paper attributed 17.2% of unexpected interruptions during a 54-day run across 16,384 H100 GPUs to HBM3 memory, the second-largest cause behind failed GPUs, a reliability burden that scales with the amount of HBM in each package. (Image credit: Micron)Share and supply outlookSK hynix leads the HBM market with a share that Counterpoint Research places at around 58%, down from a high of around 69%, and Micron overtook Samsung for second place last year. Micron began volume shipments of 36GB 12-high HBM4 earlier this year for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang saying in June that all three suppliers are qualified and in production.Analysts expect DDR5 per-wafer profitability to overtake HBM3E by the end of this year, leaving the three makers little reason to add commodity capacity when server DRAM pays nearly as well per wafer. SK hynix said last October that it had already sold its entire 2026 output, while Apacer's chief executive told investors that supply to independent module makers could fall to 30% of 2026 volumes next year. SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung has called 2027 the worst year for memory supply in the industry's history, with demand outrunning production into 2030.In response, Nvidia has raised its DGX Spark desktop from $3,999 to $4,699 and warned large customers of AI server price rises above 15%, both tied to memory. Realistically, the squeeze will loosen only under three conditions, none of them likely before new fab capacity comes online and scales up: China's CXMT ramping competitive DDR5 in volume, hybrid bonding arriving before HBM5, which SK hynix has already all but ruled out, or DDR5 profitability slipping back below HBM.Full Micron Hot Chips 2026 presentation Image 1 of 18 (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) (Image credit: Micron) Image 1 of 18 View Original Image 2 of 18 View Original Image 3 of 18 View Original Image 4 of 18 View Original Image 5 of 18 View Original Image 6 of 18 View Original Image 7 of 18 View Original Image 8 of 18 View Original Image 9 of 18 View Original Image 10 of 18 View Original Image 11 of 18 View Original Image 12 of 18 View Original Image 13 of 18 View Original Image 14 of 18 View Original Image 15 of 18 View Original Image 16 of 18 View Original Image 17 of 18 View Original Image 18 of 18 View Original

items.descriptionZh:
在Hot Chips 2026大会上，美光HBM设计架构院士Raghu Sreeramaneni揭露了一个令业界忧虑的现实：HBM（高带宽内存）相对于DDR5的硅片面积代价正在逐代扩大，且无法在不牺牲性能的前提下缩小，美光也绝不会为此放弃性能。这一技术瓶颈已成为当前内存价格飙涨的核心推手。据美光测算，相同容量下HBM所占晶圆面积约为DDR5的三倍，且这一差距随工艺代际递增——引脚速度、Bank数量、堆叠层数和裸片尺寸都在持续攀升，导致硅片开销越来越大。

从技术原理看，HBM通过极致的并行化换取带宽：HBM4单颗裸片集成256个Bank，而DDR5仅有32个；单个HBM3E裸片可输出256GB/s带宽，DDR5裸片仅约8GB/s。要达到同样的数据位宽，HBM裸片必须大幅增加数据通路、供电网络和硅通孔（TSV）所占面积。代价极其惊人：在双GPU封装中，内存占据了约90%的硅片面积，约为GPU裸片的8倍。同时HBM每比特售价约为DDR5的五倍，因此厂商将产能转向HBM时，会不成比例地压缩面向消费市场的普通DRAM供应，进而推高PC内存价格。

市场数据印证了这一冲击。2026年第一季度传统DRAM合约价环比暴涨90%至95%，第二季度再涨58%至63%。主流32GB DDR5-6000内存套装当月售价约392美元，而一年前仅为110至140美元；128GB DDR5价格突破3399美元，一年间上涨500%，欧洲市场自去年9月以来已累计上涨345%。惠普2月透露，DRAM已占其PC制造成本的35%，而一个季度前这一比例还只有15%至18%；Gartner预计2026年PC出货量将下滑超过10%。尽管第三季度涨幅放缓至13%至18%，但这并非供应改善，而是终端厂商已触及成本转嫁上限，消费者面临的价格压力并未真正缓解。

在技术演进方面，美光指出，计算性能约每两年提升三倍，而HBM带宽增速不到两倍，Sreeramaneni坦言“内存墙依然存在，甚至可能更糟”。HBM4将主机接口翻倍至2048个I/O，美光产品单引脚速率超过11Gb/s，单堆栈带宽超过2.8TB/s，均高于JEDEC HBM4标准规定的8Gb/s和2TB/s。然而这些增益全部来自更强的并行性，又反过来扩大了硅片面积差距。美光认为“到16层DRAM堆叠仍有一条可行的路径”，但超过16层后挑战巨大。SK hynix在同一会议上描述了775微米的总厚度上限，在混合键合技术普及前，堆叠层数无法突破，而该技术预计要到HBM5时代才能应用。美光计划于2027年推出的HBM4E将把逻辑基底裸片转至台积电代工工艺，这反映了AI工作负载碎片化后行业走向定制化与“分解”设计的大趋势。

热管理是另一大难题。基底裸片位于堆叠底部，承担最高速接口工作，但散热器却在顶部，因此基底最热；每增加一层，热阻就相应上升。Sreeramaneni表示，美光如今“围绕热设计架构，而非反过来”，与数年前截然不同。可靠性也随HBM用量增加而恶化：Meta在Llama 3训练论文中报告，在16,384块H100 GPU持续54天的运行中，17.2%的意外中断归因于HBM3内存，是仅次于GPU故障的第二大原因。

供应格局同样严峻。Counterpoint Research数据显示，SK hynix仍以约58%的份额领先HBM市场（低于此前约69%的高点），美光去年超越三星升至第二。美光今年早些时候已开始为Nvidia Vera Rubin平台量产出货36GB 12层HBM4；黄仁勋6月确认三家供应商均已通过认证并投产。分析师预计，DDR5每晶圆利润将在2026年底前超过HBM3E，这使得三大原厂几乎没有任何动力扩充消费级DDR5产能——服务器DRAM每晶圆的收益已接近HBM。SK hynix去年10月表示2026年产能已全部售出，Apacer CEO则警告独立模组厂商明年获得的供应可能仅为2026年出货量的30%。SK hynix CEO更将2027年称为“行业历史上内存供应最糟糕的一年”，需求超越产出将延续至2030年。Nvidia已因此将DGX Spark桌面设备价格从3999美元上调至4699美元，并警告大客户AI服务器涨价超15%。

Sreeramaneni指出，HBM与DDR5的硅片代价差距“绝对没有在改善”，而这一局面只有在三种条件下才能缓解：中国CXMT大规模量产具有竞争力的DDR5、混合键合在HBM5之前实现（SK hynix几乎已排除此可能）、或DDR5每晶圆利润重新回落到HBM之下。然而这三条路在新增晶圆厂产能真正爬坡前，都很难实质性落地。换言之，内存价格的紧张态势短期内难有转机，AI产业持续吞噬硅片资源的同时，PC与服务器用户都在为这场“内存墙”的代价买单。

items.title: Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia breaks down 88-core Vera CPU — spatial multithreading benchmarked, 1.2 TB/s SOCAMM2 memory, agentic workloads detailed, and more
items.description: Nvidia has provided more color on its Vera CPU for agentic data centers at Hot Chips 2026, showcasing the benefits of spatial multithreading and the power benefits of the LPDDR5X memory system.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter This Tom's Hardware Premium article is free to read with a Tom's Hardware account; no payment necessary. We're offering free access from August 23 to 26 so you can read all of our reporting from Hot Chips.Nvidia has spent the last several months providing key disclosures about its next-gen Vera CPU for agentic data centers, which it continued at Hot Chips 2026. Although we've already learned a lot about Vera, how it compares to AMD's next-gen Venice CPUs, and the inner workings of the Olympus core, Nvidia provided a bit more color at Hot Chips on spatial multithreading, the memory subsystem, and what types of workloads it's targeting with Vera.As a quick refresher, Vera is the first CPU with a custom Nvidia core, following up on Grace, which used a stock Arm design. It's shipping as a single, 88-core SKU, and it has some key design differences compared to Nvidia's x86 competition, most notably a multi-threading implementation that Nvidia calls spatial multi-threading, an LPDDR5X memory subsystem, and a monolithic compute die rather than using compute chiplets.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Nvidia says it's designed Vera specifically for agentic AI workloads, a category that's still being defined in terms of performance benchmarking. Many CPU-intensive tasks serve as proxies for agentic workloads (i.e., code compilation), though measuring performance across a full agentic chain is complex and inconsistent. Nvidia, in its own slides (see the end of this article), calls agentic AI the "most complex computing workload in history," after all.Nvidia provided an example of a headless browser to show the benefits of Vera, using optimized code to mimic how an agent would use a browser. Compared to the 96-core EPYC 9655P, Nvidia says Vera runs 24% faster as browser instances scale. You may like Nvidia deep dives Vera CPU for AI data centers Nvidia touts Vera CPU's single-threaded performance as its agentic AI advantage SpaceXAI will deploy standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs for Grok's agentic workloads (Image credit: Nvidia)This slide is a good demonstration of the complexities in measuring traditional workloads and applying that performance to agentic workflows. Agents will often fetch websites for information, but there are several layers where agents can trim back compared to humans; in this case, agents can run through a browsing workflow 4.5x faster by cutting things like GUI rendering, fonts, media decoding, and more. (Image credit: Nvidia)Another touchstone for agentic performance is code compilation, as agents seek out software to compile on the system. This might be the most direct benchmark of agentic AI performance with current workflows right now. Though, as previously mentioned, agentic chains are long, complex, and involve several different workloads.Once again, compared to the 96-core EPYC 9655P, Nvidia claims Vera can compile the Linux kernel 22% faster with a native AArch64 target, and 14% faster when cross-compiling for x86.Nvidia's big cores for agentic AI — another look at Olympus and how it fits into VeraNvidia reiterated the importance of the large cores inside Vera, including the large BPU, neural branch predictor, and 10-wide decode. Nvidia has previously disclosed the Olympus core architecture, which you can read about in our Vera deep dive. Broadly speaking, however, it's a wide core optimized for high single-core throughput.One of the more interesting design points of Vera is spatial multi-threading, which Nvidia described in more detail during its Hot Chips 2026. In short, Nvidia separates core resources on two pipelines, though data and cache can move between threads as needed. To demonstrate the benefit, Nvidia shared the results from SPEC CPU 2017 intrate that you can see below. What to read next Nvidia has ‘shipped hundreds of thousands of Grace standalone servers’ Nvidia offers restricted access to Vera CPU in first round of Linux benchmarks AMD fires back at Nvidia, claiming 256-core Zen 6 'Venice' CPU beats Vera by 3.3x in rack-level performance (Image credit: Nvidia)This shows the "noisy neighbor" effect. Nvidia measured single-core performance and then measured the same workload with another thread active. Nvidia's data shows that Vera is less concerned with the neighboring thread, whereas a "traditional CPU" sees a larger slowdown. Nvidia didn't clarify which CPU it's comparing Vera to here, however.Nvidia's slide does a good job illustrating, but it's worth noting the difference compared to traditional SMT nonetheless. With traditional SMT, resources are time-sliced between threads, leading to gaps between BP and decode, as illustrated in the slide. With spatial multithreading in Vera, threads are still fighting for resources within the core. However, spatial multithreading allows Nvidia to deal with the demand of neighboring threads in a deterministic way, leading to a more consistent downturn in per-core performance when the second thread is working.Nvidia's second-gen Scalable Coherency Fabric (SCF) moves data across the die. Nvidia didn't provide any new disclosures around SCF at Hot Chips, but you can see how the fabric is laid out in the slide below. Centralized Coherency Switch Nodes (CSNs) connect the cores to pools of L3 cache totaling 164 MB and the broader memory subsystem. (Image credit: Nvidia)At a system level, one of the more interesting choices Nvidia made was to use LPDDR5X as opposed to traditional RDIMMs, a choice that it was only able to make due to the serviceable SOCAMM2 design. Nvidia includes eight SOCAMM2 slots per Vera CPU on a board, offering up to 1.5 TB of capacity with 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth. (Image credit: Nvidia)LPDDR5X can deliver transfer rates higher than DDR5 RDIMMs, at least compared to single-rank DIMMs. However, it seems the driving force behind LPDDR5X wasn't performance but rather power consumption. One of the pillars of Vera, according to Nvidia's Hot Chips presentation, was to deliver a CPU for power-limited data centers. Micron says its LPDDR5X consumes about a third of the power compared to a traditional RDIMM. (Image credit: Nvidia)Nvidia demonstrated that point a little differently, using bandwidth per watt as a point of comparison between the LPDDR5X system in Vera and traditional RDIMMs. This illustration does the job, though it could be a bit misleading, measuring power draw against peak bandwidth.Nvidia tells us that a fully loaded memory system with Vera consumes between 30W and 40W, with 1.5 TB at 9600 MT/s. Power demands for RDIMMs vary wildly depending on capacity, channels, and transfer rate, though power consumption can easily climb over 100W depending on the configuration.Although Nvidia has deployed Grace in the data center — to the tune of "hundreds of thousands" of standalone servers, apparently — Vera represents Nvidia's first big push to gobble up market share in the expanding agentic CPU market. It's highly targeted, as evidenced by the fact that Nvidia is only delivering a single 88-core SKU, and it's already being put to use in large-scale deployments, with Nvidia announcing yesterday a deployment of Vera at SpaceXAI. (Image credit: Nvidia)Nvidia has shared the slide above before, which it once again showed at Hot Chips 2026. It's normalizing per-core performance in SPEC CPU 2026 against the AMD EPYC 9755. The core differences explain the big disparity in numbers; in reality, Vera led in overall score by 3%. Regardless, this is the slide Nvidia is using to pitch Vera, claiming it offers a big improvement in the workloads that are most relevant for agentic AI.The most formidable opponent for Vera isn't Turin, however. It's Venice, which AMD launched in June, and Diamond Rapids, which Intel detailed just moments after Nvidia left the stage. Vera has a lot of interesting talking points already, but it'll be interesting to watch how Nvidia scales (or doesn't scale) its data center CPU business over the next few generations. Perhaps we'll see the firm double down on these agentic workflows, or maybe concessions and product segmentation to appeal to hyperscalers. Time will tell.Full Nvidia Vera Hot Chips 2026 presentation Image 1 of 31 (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) (Image credit: Nvidia) Image 1 of 31 View Original Image 2 of 31 View Original Image 3 of 31 View Original Image 4 of 31 View Original Image 5 of 31 View Original Image 6 of 31 View Original Image 7 of 31 View Original Image 8 of 31 View Original Image 9 of 31 View Original Image 10 of 31 View Original Image 11 of 31 View Original Image 12 of 31 View Original Image 13 of 31 View Original Image 14 of 31 View Original Image 15 of 31 View Original Image 16 of 31 View Original Image 17 of 31 View Original Image 18 of 31 View Original Image 19 of 31 View Original Image 20 of 31 View Original Image 21 of 31 View Original Image 22 of 31 View Original Image 23 of 31 View Original Image 24 of 31 View Original Image 25 of 31 View Original Image 26 of 31 View Original Image 27 of 31 View Original Image 28 of 31 View Original Image 29 of 31 View Original Image 30 of 31 View Original Image 31 of 31 View Original

items.titleZh: Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia breaks down 88-core Vera CPU — spatial multithreading benchmarked, 1.2 TB/s SOCAMM2 memory, agentic workloads detailed, and more
items.descriptionZh:
Nvidia在Hot Chips 2026大会上进一步披露了其下一代Vera CPU的更多细节，这款芯片专为“代理型AI”（agentic AI）数据中心设计。Vera是Nvidia首款采用完全自研核心架构的服务器CPU，此前的Grace使用的是标准Arm设计。Vera以单一88核心SKU形式出货，采用单片计算die而非时下流行的chiplet方案，并在多线程和内存子系统上做出了与x86竞品截然不同的设计选择。

Vera的核心基于Nvidia的Olympus架构，主打大尺寸物理核心，配备大型分支预测单元（BPU）、神经分支预测器以及10路解码，核心思路是最大化单线程吞吐量。在Hot Chips上，Nvidia重点介绍了其独特的“空间多线程”（Spatial Multi-Threading）技术。与传统SMT通过时间切片共享执行资源不同，Vera将核心资源划分为两条独立流水线，数据与缓存可以根据需要在线程之间移动。这种设计能以确定性的方式处理相邻线程的资源争抢，从而显著减轻“吵闹邻居”效应。Nvidia展示的SPEC CPU 2017 intrate测试表明，当第二个线程同时运行时，Vera的单核性能下降幅度远小于传统CPU，性能表现更可预测。

内存子系统是Vera另一大亮点。Nvidia没有采用服务器常见的RDIMM，而是选择了LPDDR5X，这得益于其可维护的SOCAMM2模块设计。每个Vera CPU搭配8个SOCAMM2插槽，最大支持1.5TB容量和1.2TB/s的带宽。Nvidia强调，选择LPDDR5X的根本原因并非峰值性能，而是功耗——在1.5TB容量、9600MT/s速率下，满配内存系统功耗仅为30至40W，而传统RDIMM配置轻松超过100W。美光数据也显示LPDDR5X功耗约为RDIMM的三分之一。这顺应了Vera面向功率受限数据中心的设计目标。

针对代理型AI工作负载，Nvidia给出了两个具体对比数据：在与AMD 96核EPYC 9655P的对比中，Vera在无头浏览器场景下（模拟代理抓取网页信息）性能高出24%；编译Linux内核时，原生AArch64编译快22%，交叉编译x86版本快14%。代理型AI是当前定义尚不清晰的复杂工作负载，Nvidia甚至称其为“史上最复杂的计算工作负载”，因此这些基准测试只是评估代理链条中的片段。此外，Nvidia将SPEC CPU 2026的每核性能归一化后对比AMD EPYC 9755，Vera整体得分领先3%，不过核心架构差异导致不同负载下的成绩分歧明显。

Vera是Nvidia首次大规模进军代理型CPU市场。此前Grace已部署了“数十万台”独立服务器，而Vera则表现出高度聚焦的策略——仅提供一个88核SKU。就在大会前一天，Nvidia宣布Vera已在SpaceXAI完成部署，用于Grok的代理型工作负载。然而，Vera面临的最强劲对手并非EPYC Turin，而是AMD于6月发布的256核Venice，以及Intel紧随Nvidia之后披露的Diamond Rapids。Vera凭借大核心、空间多线程和低功耗内存等差异化特性，试图在代理型AI的早期市场中建立优势；未来Nvidia是否会坚持这一细分路线，或向超大规模云厂商妥协而调整产品线，仍有待观察。

items.title: SpaceXAI will deploy standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs for Grok's agentic workloads — will use optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 in space with Starmind satellite
items.description: Nvidia claims the chip completes agentic, reinforcement learning, and data processing tasks up to 1.8 times faster than x86 processors.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia's 88-core Vera chip will be getting put to work for Elon Musk twice over, first and foremost as the standalone CPU orchestrating Grok's AI agents in SpaceXAI's data centers and, from the fourth quarter of 2027, inside the company's first Starmind satellite. Nvidia announced the deployment yesterday, making SpaceXAI the second hyperscaler after Meta to commit to Vera outside full Vera Rubin racks, with Musk supplying the launch window in a post on X. Nvidia claims the chip completes agentic, reinforcement learning, and data processing tasks up to 1.8 times faster than x86 processors, but that figure hasn't been independently verified.Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc)Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecksLeading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and SamsungASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examinedChinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examinedAgents spend much of their runtime off the GPU. A model that writes code, for example, calls tools, queries databases, and parses results by leaning on the host CPU between every inference pass; idle GPUs waiting on that work are wasted capital. "Vera gives us the CPU performance and memory bandwidth to run enormous amounts of orchestration, code, and data processing while keeping GPUs doing what they do best," Mike Nicolls, president of SpaceXAI, said in the release.SpaceX, in partnership with Nvidia, has designed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system for launch to orbit in Q4 next year, with significant scale in 2028 https://t.co/qdDq8YBkzlAugust 24, 2026Meta was the first company to announce a large-scale standalone Vera deployment, confirming in February that it would run Grace-only servers in production with Vera to follow as soon as 2027. Nvidia has since disclosed shipping hundreds of thousands of standalone Grace servers and more than 2.5 million Grace CPUs in total, and the SpaceXAI deal extends that dominance directly into territory held by AMD's EPYC and Intel's Xeon lines.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Vera pairs 88 custom Olympus cores on a monolithic die with spatial multithreading and LPDDR5X memory delivering up to 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth. Nvidia's performance claims for the chip remain contested, and AMD has countered that its 256-core Zen 6 Venice processors beat Vera by 3.3 times in rack-level performance. Neither company disclosed how many Vera CPUs SpaceXAI will deploy, the value of the deal, or when the data center rollout begins; the only date attached to the announcement is the satellite launch window.Musk said earlier this month that Starmind launches would begin in 2027, and his X post following the press release narrowed that to the fourth quarter, with what he described as significant scale-up following in 2028. The terrestrial NVL72 combines 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs in a fully liquid-cooled rack, and an orbital version has to be reworked for radiation exposure, heat rejection through radiators rather than facility water loops, launch vibration, and the absence of any hands-on servicing. You may like Nvidia has ‘shipped hundreds of thousands of Grace standalone servers’ Elon Musk says SpaceX will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs 'because they are the best' Nvidia deep dives Vera CPU for AI data centers SpaceXAI's first-generation AI1 satellite design carries a 120 kW compute payload, peaking at 150 kW, on a craft wider than a Boeing 747. The company has also acknowledged that orbital compute at the scale it's targeting requires significantly more chips than it currently has access to, a constraint the Vera Rubin commitment doesn't itself address. items.titleZh: SpaceXAI will deploy standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs for Grok's agentic workloads — will use optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 in space with Starmind satellite
items.descriptionZh:
Nvidia宣布，其88核Vera CPU将被SpaceXAI采用，首先是作为独立处理器在SpaceXAI数据中心中编排Grok的AI代理，其次将从2027年第四季度起搭载于该公司首颗Starmind卫星。这一部署使SpaceXAI成为继Meta之后，第二家在完整Vera Rubin机架之外承诺使用Vera的超大规模云服务商。马斯克在X平台上确认了发射窗口。Nvidia声称，该芯片在代理式AI、强化学习和数据处理任务上的完成速度可达x86处理器的1.8倍，但这一数字尚未得到独立验证。

代理式AI在工作时，大量运行时间并不在GPU上。以写代码的模型为例，每次推理之间都需要通过宿主机CPU调用工具、查询数据库并解析结果，而等待这些操作的GPU处于空闲状态，这相当于浪费资本。SpaceXAI总裁Mike Nicolls在新闻稿中表示：“Vera提供的CPU性能和内存带宽，使我们能够处理海量的编排、代码和数据任务，同时让GPU专注于它们最擅长的工作。”

Vera采用单片式设计，集成了88个定制Olympus内核，支持空间多线程技术，并配备LPDDR5X内存，可提供高达1.2TB/s的带宽。不过，Nvidia对该芯片的性能声明仍存在争议——AMD此前回应称，其256核Zen 6 Venice处理器在机架级性能上比Vera高出3.3倍。两家公司均未披露SpaceXAI将部署多少颗Vera CPU，也未公布交易金额以及数据中心落地的具体时间，唯一的日期信息是卫星发射窗口。

Meta是首家宣布大规模部署独立Vera的公司，今年2月就已确认将在生产环境中运行仅采用Grace芯片的服务器，并计划最快于2027年引入Vera。Nvidia随后披露，已出货数十万台独立Grace服务器，Grace CPU总出货量超过250万颗。SpaceXAI的这笔交易将这种主导地位直接延伸至AMD EPYC和Intel Xeon占据的传统领地。

SpaceX与Nvidia合作设计了一套针对太空优化的Vera Rubin NVL72系统，计划于明年第四季度发射入轨，并在2028年实现显著规模扩展。地面版NVL72将一个完全液冷机架中组合了72颗Rubin GPU和36颗Vera CPU，而轨道版必须针对辐射暴露、通过散热器而非设施水循环进行热量排散、发射振动以及无人维护等条件重新设计。SpaceXAI的第一代AI1卫星设计携带120kW计算载荷，峰值可达150kW，其机身宽度超过波音747。

马斯克本月初曾表示Starmind发射将于2027年开始，在他于新闻稿发布后的X帖文中，将时间进一步明确为第四季度，并称随后将在2028年实现大规模扩展。此外，SpaceXAI也承认，其目标规模的轨道计算需要的芯片数量远超当前可获得的资源，而这一约束并不会因采用Vera Rubin而得到解决。

items.content: Alabama’s attorney general issued a subpoena to OpenAI on Monday as part of an investigation into how one of its AI agents escaped a supposedly secure testing environment and autonomously hacked another company last month.The investigation seeks to determine whether OpenAI’s safety practices violated state consumer protection laws and pose a risk to Alabama citizens, the AG’s office said in a statement.“This AI lab leak showed that Alabamians’ and Americans’ worst fears about artificial intelligence are not just theoretical,” said Attorney General Steve Marshall. “Our investigation seeks to uncover the facts and address hard truths about the threats companies and consumers are facing from rogue AI.”Marshall was among 15 red state attorneys general who wrote to OpenAI asking it to preserve records about the Hugging Face hack last month. The subpoena adds to mounting scrutiny over safety practices at frontier labs in the wake of both that incident and other episodes subsequently uncovered elsewhere, including Anthropic and Meta.
